driver: Each unit's call rests on the expected time a rule keeps it stopped in a coming window, where the rule restarts a fixed timer at every event and the only record of past events misses them at a rate that depends on each event's size and on the recording equipment in range that day; the stopped time is the union of the timers, so the missed events shorten spells, split them and erase whole days in a way no proportional raise restores, and one class of equipment counts for a fraction of a standard unit that no document states and that shows only in how weak the events recorded under it are.
driver_concrete: Kestrel Coast Ground Handling carries a relief ramp crew at a station whose expected lightning stand-down in the 2026-27 wet season is over 25 hours. The stand-down is the union of the 15 minute intervals opened by every ground stroke within 8 km, and the national network's archive locates a stroke with a chance that rises with its peak current and with the sensors up that day (a filed table); the hours are rebuilt by replaying the timer on the well-covered days thinned to each station's sensor count and reading each recorded day by its size, with a legacy receiver worth 0.32 of a standard sensor (fitted from the amplitudes of the strokes located on its days) and the region's response to the shelf index carried to the bureau's outlook value.
stump: The careful but hurried route (the located strokes' hours, or those hours raised by the share of strokes missed, or the missed strokes put back between the located ones; every sensor counted alike) files a relief crew at Callory Downs alone, or on the proportional raise at Callory Downs, Penrow Sound, Mornay Inlet and Tarrick Tableland with Weymoor Gap left out; the hours stump lost alone leaves Callory Downs only and the legacy stump lost alone drops Weymoor Gap (17.2 hours against 28.6); each stump pushed past its fitted value alone files a wrong call too (the hours raised in proportion with the worth fitted: a crew everywhere but Yanda Creek; a legacy receiver worth nothing: a fifth crew at Burrel Bay, 28.9 hours), and a calibration cut at any size of well-covered day files a wrong call.
results: R1 the located strokes set against the sensor log, station-day by station-day; R2 the peak-current law of ground strokes through the filed detection curve and the share located at each sensor count; R3 what a legacy receiver adds, in standard sensors, and the ground strokes an average season brings each station; R4 the hours an average season stands each station down, from the timer replayed on the well-covered days thinned to each sensor count; R5 every correction tested on the well-covered days thinned to two and three sensors; R6 the region's response to the shelf index and this season against an average one; R7 each station's expected stand-down hours this season and the relief crew call; R8 how strong a season, as a per cent of an average one, puts each station at the line
one_fact_test: the most useful sentence (missed strokes shorten stand-downs, split them and erase whole days, so recorded hours do not scale with the share located) leaves the replay to design, the recorded day size to condition on and the days that left no record to estimate; it rescues R4 and R5 on the reflex route (2 of 8) and 19 rubric points with Weymoor Gap still wrong; the legacy receiver sentence rescues R3 alone

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a rare-event level at an unmeasured unit transferred from a measured neighbour whose events each drew on only the part of it below a threshold that moved from event to event, while the unmeasured unit lies almost wholly below that threshold: transferring by size undersizes it, a ratio read at a typical event oversizes it because the largest events drew on nearly all of the neighbour, and only transferring every event at its own threshold lands the level.

lineage.driver: A storage buffer that captures a discharge until it is full empties only through a receiving channel whose spare capacity vanishes for one to several days after each wet event, so in a run of events the buffer meets the next one still partly full; counting each event against an empty buffer, or a buffer emptied at its outlet's rated pace, understates how often it spills, and only replaying the record with the outlet bounded by the receiving channel's spare capacity, read from that channel's own record, prices the size the limit needs.
lineage.driver_concrete: Clay Street's tank is pumped out into the Southside interceptor at the plant headworks, and the Southside plant, its sewershed full of groundwater and inflow, takes its 140 MGD hydraulic limit for one to four days after most storms from March to June; the Northside tank, whose plant has room within hours, empties at its pumps' rating and its overflows replay exactly that way, but Clay Street's pumps can only send what Southside has room for, so in a wet spell the tank meets the next storm still full and the 26 MG alternative that clears four events at its pumps' rating leaves 6.8 a year; only the 38 MG tank, at 2.9, meets the decree.
lineage.stump: A competent solver replays Outfall 014's metered overflows through each tank pumped out at its station's rated dewatering flow (the continuous simulation the decree evaluates by, which reproduces the Northside tank's overflows since 2020) and selects Alternative B, the 26 MG tank, at 2.8 events a year; the step that lands it there is taking the pumps' rating as the pace the tank empties, when it empties into the Southside interceptor at the headworks of a plant that sits at its 140 MGD limit for days after wet-season storms, so only a replay bounded by Southside's own headroom hour by hour shows the 20 MG tank at 6.8 events and selects Alternative C, the 38 MG tank, at 2.9.
lineage.answer: Select Alternative C, the 38 MG tank: it leaves Outfall 014 2.9 untreated overflow events a year, where the 26 MG Alternative B leaves 6.8.

lineage.driver_concrete: The road service classes a gully crossing on the triggering storms a season at its source area (3 or more: automatic barrier; 1 to 3: seasonal patrol; under 1: signs). The governing gauge is an unheated tipping bucket at the road station below: it loses water while it tips, more the harder it rains (a true 100 mm an hour reads 20 per cent low on the smaller bucket), which the monthly storage gauge account measures only when the loss is fitted on the rate; a source's cloudbursts differ from its gauge's by a factor the yearly rainfall does not carry (Rio Marden 1.38 against a rainfall ratio of 1.06), which the radar's pixel pairs measure storm by storm although the radar's own depths undercount; and on hail days the funnel holds the ice and the bucket tips its melt for an hour or two, so the tips miss a quarter of those storms' 60-minute maximum, which the detector's ten-minute record of when precipitation fell puts back.
